conditions.text: C1. Content: a nipātana is undertaken only where some general rule would otherwise apply, so within its own scope it blocks that rule (the regular form is not also correct there). The rival view, that nipātanas need not block, is rejected as against the Bhāṣya.

quotes.quote: अत्र भाष्यानुसाराद्बाधकान्येव निपातनानि भवन्तीति पक्ष आश्रितः

conditions.text: C2. Scope: the sūtra must state a form ready-made (Kāśikā “निपात्यते/निपात्यन्ते”, or a list of forms valid exactly as spoken). A time rule or a saṃjñā that makes listed words correct by another route is not a nipātana.

quotes.quote: भविष्यति काले गम्यादयः शब्दाः साधवो भवन्ति। प्रत्ययस्यैव भविष्यत्कालता विधीयते न प्रकृतेः।
भपदसंज्ञाधिकारे विधानात् तेन मुखेन साधुत्वमयस्मयादीनां विधीयते।

conditions.text: C3. What blocking means, in a commentator's words; and its absence: where the text says the regular form is also used, PIS 119 does no work.

quotes.quote: समुदायपाठस्य च प्रयोजनं विषयनियमः — स्त्रियामेव, तत्र ङीप्प्रत्यय एव, नान्यदा।
न पुनरयमादेशः शिरःशब्दस्य, सोऽपि हि छन्दसि प्रयुज्यत एव

conditions.text: C4. Optional nipātanas: where the sūtra itself keeps the regular form as an option, blocking and not blocking give the same forms (see the “unsure” members). Where commentators invoke the rival maxim “अबाधकान्यपि निपातनानि” it is on sūtras that are not in this firing list.

not_licensed.word: a nipātana stands against the general rules that would give another form
not_licensed.why: The Kāśikā makes शीर्षन् a separate word, explicitly not a substitute for शिरस्, because शिरस् is also used in the Veda — so nothing is blocked (C3). (The Kaumudī instead reads it as a substitute, “शिरःशब्दस्य शीर्षन् स्यात्”, which is an ādeśa rule, not a nipātana — PIS 119 is not needed on either reading.)

quotes.quote: शीर्षन्निति शब्दान्तरं शिरःशब्देन समानार्थं छन्दसि विषये निपात्यते, न पुनरयमादेशः शिरःशब्दस्य, सोऽपि हि छन्दसि प्रयुज्यत एव

unsure.word: a nipātana stands against the general rules that would give another form
unsure.why: Optional nipātana: the sūtra itself (वा / अन्यतरस्याम् / उदीचाम्) keeps the regular form beside the nipātana, so the question PIS 119 settles — does a nipātana shut out the regular form? — gets the same answer (both forms) whether nipātanas block or not. In the nipātana's own option the regular rule is set aside, so a credit is defensible; it is not needed to read the sūtra. Policy call for Harsha.

groups.note: 6.1.27 (शृतं पाके) is licensed: the Kāśikā makes its विभाषा a fixed one (quoted below), so the nipātana does block श्राण/श्रपित for milk and oblation. 3.3.78 (अन्तर्घनः) is licensed although the Kāśikā words it as a vidhi: the irregular घन stands against अन्तर्घात, which the Kāśikā gives only outside the meaning. 7.2.18 is licensed; note the Kāśikā on 7.2.28 lets a later option override its स्वान्त — a nipātana can itself be overridden; that does not touch the credit here.

note_quotes.quote: व्यवस्थितविभाषा चेयम्, तेन क्षीरहविषोर्नित्यं शृभावो भवति
अन्तःपूर्वाद् हन्तेरप् प्रत्ययो भवति, घनादेशश्च भवति देशेऽभिधेये।
